transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Recording: yes (audio)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood PM), Amina Torres (CEO, StellarCart), Elliot Park (CTO), Ravi Kapoor (Head of Growth)

Auto-summary (generated): Informal on-record interview focusing on StellarCart's use of Redwood Inference, migration from hosted to dedicated for peak holiday traffic, and measurable improvements in latency and unit cost. Editorial next steps and legal sign-off discussed.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — this is meant to be pretty conversational, we wanna capture your story for the Redwood customer spotlight. Amina, want to kick us off with a quick bit about how StellarCart started?
[00:18] Amina Torres: Yeah absolutely, um so StellarCart began in 2020, we were a small two-person team, uh building a headless e-comm layer for boutique retailers. We realized fast that the recommender and search experiences were the thing that actually made or broke conversions for our customers. So we.. we started experimenting with embeddings and reranking and eventually integrated LLM-driven product copy, product titles, that sort of thing.
[00:40] Elliot Park: And.. the early experiments were messy, we used a few hosted endpoints, latency was okay until load spikes, and then it became, you know, a real customer-visible problem.
[00:50] Ravi Kapoor: That was the holiday 2024 spike — page loads were fine but the personalized rec block would lag, and conversion dropped about 7% in our A/B. So we needed a more predictable inference plan.
[01:05] Maya Patel: That makes sense. Jordan and I were talking earlier — the story we want to highlight is the move from hosted to Redwood Dedicated to handle predictable throughput for holiday peaks. Could you walk us through the evaluation? Why Redwood vs the others?
[01:20] Amina Torres: Sure. We evaluated CartFlow and NimbusShop and did a couple of bench runs. The tiebreaker was actually the operational visibility — we liked Redwood's console for token-level cost breakdowns. Also the ability to pin model versions and the routing fallback behavior mattered; during a simulated outage, Redwood's fallback to a small-quantized variant kept things live.
[01:40] Elliot Park: The perf numbers were super persuasive. On our POC tests with our typical request distribution — short product titles plus longer recommendation contexts — average token latency dropped from ~450ms to ~120ms after tuning the batch size and enabling prefix KV caching. Now in production it's consistently under 150ms for 95th.
[02:00] Jordan Lee: Quick follow up — did you use Redwood Optimize suggestions or did your infra team tune things directly?
[02:07] Elliot Park: We used the Optimize recommendations as a starting point. The suggested quantization profile saved CPU cycles without a hit to human-verified quality. Then we iterated with Redwood SE on batching configs. There was one awkward moment where the k-v cache was referred to in docs as k-v cash in an auto transcript — tiny typo, but we laughed.
[02:25] Ravi Kapoor: Yeah, and from a cost perspective — we measured around 30% lower cost per 1k inference tokens once we moved to dedicated with smart batching and caching, which helped our unit economics for mid-market customers.
[02:40] Maya Patel: That's a great stat for the case study. For the podcast, do you remember a specific anecdote from the first successful holiday weekend after the migration?
[02:50] Amina Torres: Oh yes, we had a retailer who'd been nervous about CPS — we pushed the new stack on Friday night and by Saturday they emailed us saying their personalization CTR was up and they hadn't had a single complaint about speed. The team celebrated with pizza.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: Love that. We'll want to capture that line as a quote — subject to approvals of course.
[03:12] Amina Torres: Yep, legal will need to sign off but happy to provide a quote.
[03:17] [00:03:20] Elliot Park: There was also the security side — we integrated Redwood Private for a couple of enterprise customers who needed VPC peering and KMS integration. The Redwood team helped with the KMS rotation plan and audit logs. That was important for our Fortune 500 pilot.
[03:40] Maya Patel: Did you run into any bumps on the VPC/on-prem setup?
[03:44] Elliot Park: A few network ACL bits — the first run we forgot to open the health-check port, so the orchestration failed a probe and triggered a retry loop. Redwood SE helped walk us through the firewall rules. Also the SSO setup had a small hiccup — SAML metadata URL was stale on our side so it tripped the login flow. Took one afternoon to fix.
[04:05] Ravi Kapoor: From a go-to-market angle, the ability to offer a predictable SLA helped us close two deals in Q1 2026 where previously customers asked for too much margin on price. The dedicated contract with predictable throughput and burst capacity reduced buyer friction.
[04:20] [00:04:30] Jordan Lee: We're going to include some of those commercial outcomes in the case study. Quick question on numbers: can someone confirm the production 95th percentile latency figure and the percent cost improvement we can quote?
[04:40] Elliot Park: Production 95th is 145ms right now for our inference requests. Cost improvement vs baseline hosted run was about 30% lower per 1k tokens; I'll send the exact spreadsheet.
[04:52] Maya Patel: Great, we'll cite those and reference the spreadsheet Jordan will attach.
[04:56] [00:05:00] Amina Torres: One more thing — we appreciated the Redwood rollouts features, the canary deploys saved us from a bad model weight push. The automatic fallback moved traffic back to a safe variant when we saw quality regressions.
[05:15] Maya Patel: Nice. For the marketing piece, we usually put together a 12-minute highlight reel, plus 30-60s social cuts and a blog post with an executive quote. Is that still the preferred format for you?
[05:30] Amina Torres: Yes that's ideal. Also if you could send the transcript and a few proposed quote snippets that would speed approvals.
[05:37] Jordan Lee: We'll do that. Legal question — anything time-sensitive on your side for approvals?
[05:42] Amina Torres: Legal is traveling next week, so if possible aim for sign-off by mid-October. Otherwise it may slip.
[05:50] Ravi Kapoor: We can escalate internally to be quicker; I'll own chasing legal.
[05:55] [00:06:00] Maya Patel: Awesome. A few quick clarifying questions so our case study is accurate: which Redwood product did you finalize on — Dedicated or Private?
[06:07] Elliot Park: Primarily Dedicated for most workloads, Private for two enterprise customers who required VPC and KMS. We kept hosted for internal staging.
[06:17] Jordan Lee: And model catalog — were you using an open model or a Redwood-curated one?
[06:21] Elliot Park: We used a Redwood-curated open model (quantized variant) — the verified perf profile made it an easy choice.
[06:27] [00:06:30] Amina Torres: Now for the fun part — I get asked how founders choose partners. For us it was dev experience + predictability. Redwood's SDKs let our engineers iterate quickly, and the console gave product folks line-of-sight into token spend which sold this internally.
[06:45] Maya Patel: Do you recall any internal objections you had to overcome when deciding to commit to dedicated capacity?
[06:50] Ravi Kapoor: Yes — finance was worried about reserved spend. We put together a three-month pilot with burst options and a usage-based runway to build trust. Demonstrating the 30% cost improvement in our pilot convinced them.
[07:05] [00:07:20] Jordan Lee: On the recording side, we'll want a few short soundbites — Amina, a 2-sentence summary on why you chose Redwood; Elliot, a 1-sentence technical takeaway; Ravi, a 1-sentence commercial outcome. Can you give those now informal? We can polish later.
[07:34] Amina Torres: Sure — "We chose Redwood because it gave us predictable performance at scale and a transparent cost story — that let us sleep during holiday peaks."
[07:44] Elliot Park: "The technical takeaway is that caching and smart batching reduced tail latency and kept quality stable across variants."
[07:54] Ravi Kapoor: "Commercially, it unlocked better conversion during peak traffic and lowered our per-user inference cost."
[08:01] Maya Patel: Perfect — we'll use those as starting points for the release.
[08:05] [00:08:10] Amina Torres: Small caveat on quoting — we prefer calls for approval on any numbers; safe to say 'about 30%'.
[08:15] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll mark the numbers as approximate until we get sign-off.
[08:20] [00:08:30] Jordan Lee: Anything else technical worth calling out for the readers? Any gotchas?
[08:35] Elliot Park: For teams adopting inference at scale — watch your tokenization strategy. We had one case where a poorly constructed prompt exploded token usage and spiked costs. Also sequence length distribution matters a lot for kernel selection — short queries and long contexts behave differently.
[08:55] [00:09:00] Ravi Kapoor: And operationally, observability is key — Redwood Console's per-route dashboards made it easy to spot bad prompts and route them to a cheaper variant.
[09:08] Jordan Lee: Good notes. We'll include a short 'lessons learned' box in the blog.
[09:12] [00:09:20] Maya Patel: Last administrative bits — we'll send the recording raw file and a proposed set of quotes within 48 hours. Action items we'll track in the CRM. Anything else on PR or embargo?
[09:30] Amina Torres: No embargo, but please send the draft to our comms lead first.
[09:34] Maya Patel: Who's the comms lead?
[09:36] Amina Torres: That's Sofia Martinez — email sofia@stellarcart.com.
[09:40] [00:09:50] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll get the draft out by Friday.
[09:53] Ravi Kapoor: Also can you include a short timeline graphic showing the migration steps? That helps our execs.
[09:58] Maya Patel: Yep, Jordan can produce that.
[10:02] [00:10:10] (laughter)
[10:05] Amina Torres: Okay I'm happy to help with any edits. This has been fun.
[10:09] Maya Patel: Great — thanks so much for your time. We'll follow up with the draft and next steps.
[10:15] [00:10:20] (meeting winds down; casual banter)
